text:
incident-bot: ALERT — p99 tail latency > SLO for streaming-read route in eu-west2 (observed 2.1s, SLO 600ms). paging on-call (alice.ops). :rotating_light:

alice.ops: seeing p95 spike too, primarily for sessions routed through VPC egress path A. dashboard: https://redwood.example/obs/streams/route/streaming-read/eu-west2

ben.neteng: tagging in — I see elevated TCP retransmits on nodes in az-b (packetloss ~0.5-1%). DNS latency also increased for requests to nat-gateway-a.

carla-sre: streaming stalls are correlated w/ TLS handshake tail spikes. p99 for handshake time jumped to ~1100ms. logs show repeated SYN-ACK retransmits.

alice.ops: initial mitigation attempted: scaled up streaming pool (autoscale +40%) at T+2m, no improvement to tail. rolling-restart of proxies at T+6m, partial drop in error budget for a subset but p99 still > 1s.

dave-prod: customer impact — a handful of larger customers saw degraded UX for long-run streams; support ticket #INC-4829 opened. Frank from Acme noted repeated timeouts. @erin-support fyi.

erin-support: escalated to account team, replying to the customer: "we're investigating a cross-zone networking issue, will update in 10m".

jessica-eng: quick check — kernel conntrack on egress nodes is within normal ranges. CPU/GPU not saturated. This looks network-path related. Can neteng confirm NAT ephemeral exhaustion?

ben.neteng: ephemeral ports look fine. But NAT metrics show sudden jump in connection churn through nat-gw-a. Route table shows more traffic being routed via nat-gw-a due to transient flap in the bgp session to nat-gw-b.

sam-oncall: oncall handoff in 30m. Alice, can you summarize current mitigations and temp workarounds for the handoff note?

alice.ops: summary for handoff:
- Impact: p95/p99 latency spikes for streaming-read in eu-west2; some streaming stalls and reconnects.
- Observed cause: cross-zone egress path shifted to nat-gw-a causing higher packet loss and TLS handshake tail latency. BGP flap to nat-gw-b appears to have rerouted flows.
- Actions taken: scaled pool, restarted proxies, applied ephemeral port tuning on a few nodes, increased keepalive on streaming front-door, engaged neteng to check nat-gw.
- Open mitigation options: (1) force route pinning to nat-gw-b for critical customers, (2) failover to dedicated egress path (az-local NAT), (3) temporarily increase handshake retransmit timeout / enable TCP fastopen fallback.

ben.neteng: running a controlled traffic pin to nat-gw-b for a small subset of flows to see if packetloss drops. Doing that now for prefix 10.48.0.0/16 -> route via nat-gw-b.

carla-sre: adding playbook link: https://redwood.runbooks/streaming/tail-latency-networking. Also posting quick commands:
```
# check tcp retransmits
sudo ss -s
# nat gw metrics
curl -s https://metrics.internal/nat-gw-a | jq '.retransmits, .ephemeral_count'
```

alice.ops: ben — can you confirm metrics after route pinning?

ben.neteng: update: after pinning, packet loss on flows routed to nat-gw-b dropped to 0.02%, TLS handshake p99 for the pinned subset dropped from ~1100ms -> ~220ms. Overall p99 for the route improved to ~750ms (still above SLO).

dave-prod: good progress. Can we expand pinning to 50% of traffic for the streaming-read route? Need to coordinate to avoid overloading nat-gw-b.

ben.neteng: expanding to 50% now. Watching retransmit and CPU.

carla-sre: noticed that some sessions still hit streaming stalls after pinning — likely sessions that have cached upstream endpoints that still map to nat-gw-a. We might need to invalidate some prefix caches or force a reconnect.

alice.ops: suggestion: trigger soft reconnect for affected sessions (clients will resume). jessica, can your team push a soft reconnect to the long-lived session manager for customers above threshold?

jessica-eng: yes, can push a soft-reconnect to sessions > 60s idle windows and ones with > 5 consecutive stalled frames. Rolling that now. Command: `POST /admin/sessions/reconnect?min_stall=5`

frank-customer: thanks — I see stream resumed for a few users. still slow for long conversations (multi-minute). any ETA?

alice.ops: current ETA for broader mitigation: 15-20m to finish expansion and session reconnects, then monitor for SLO recovery. If not recovered, we will failover to az-local NAT which is higher-cost but stable.

ben.neteng: note — BGP flap root cause: a neighbor on nat-gw-b had transient control-plane CPU spike (provider side). Working with provider to validate stability. If they cannot guarantee, we'll plan permanent shift to az-local NAT for critical pools.

sam-oncall: handing oncall to @sam-oncall in 28m. alice — please drop final state + runbook links into the handoff document.

alice.ops: done. Pasting runbook snippet: "If cross-zone NAT causes streaming tail, prefer route pin to stable gateway, soft reconnect sessions, and escalate to provider for BGP stability. If unresolved after 30m, fail over to az-local NAT and schedule postmortem."

carla-sre: adding note to incident timeline. Also capturing packet samples and tcpdump for later RCA: `tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w /tmp/nat-a-sample.pcap`

ben.neteng: metric update at T+18m: overall p99 now 420ms after 50% pin + reconnects. p95 back to ~180ms. Looks like mitigation effective.

erin-support: updating customers: "We implemented targeted routing and session reconnects; performance improving and we continue to monitor. We'll share a write-up."

alice.ops: closing notes for handoff: continue to monitor p99 for next 2 hours, keep neteng on standby, prepare for az-local failover if metrics regress. tagging on-call. :white_check_mark:

sam-oncall: acknowledged. I'll take 2h watch and post updates. thx all — great coord.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity downgraded to S2 (customer-impact reduced), incident channel: #incident-1768932123. Postmortem assigned to carla-sre, due in 72h.
